questions.question:
**Direction: In the following sentence, an idiom is highlighted. Select the alternative which best describes its use in the sentence.**

He got a job in the Railways __through the back door__

options.text: Entered the office through the back entrance
The main door is under repair
In an indirect or unfair way

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** In an indirect or unfair way.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom** "through the back door" **is **option 4: "In an indirect or unfair way."**
 
• The idiom **"through the back door" **is commonly **used to describe a situation where someone gets something, such as a job, promotion, or opportunity, in an indirect or unfair way, often by using personal connections or influence.** The person may not have met the usual qualifications or gone through the standard selection process.
 
• For example, if someone says **"He got the job through the back door,"** it means that he did not get the job on merit, but rather through some kind of personal influence or unfair advantage.
 
• In the given sentence, the speaker is saying that the person got a job in the Railways through the back door, which implies that the person did not go through the usual selection process, but instead used some kind of personal influence or connections to secure the job.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**, "Entered the office through the back entrance," is a literal interpretation of the idiom and does not convey the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 2**, "Without appearing to others," is not related to the idiom and is not a commonly used expression.
 
• **Option 3,** "The main door is under repair," is a possible interpretation of the literal meaning of the words "through the back door," but it does not fit the context of the sentence, which is about securing a job in an indirect or unfair way.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.**

The blue embroidered saree is no doubt an ________ piece of handwork, but because of its _______ price no one was ready to buy it.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Exquisite; exorbitant.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first blank requires an **adjective **that** describes the saree as a high-quality piece of handwork.**
 
• The word "**exquisite**" means **extremely beautiful and delicate, and fits the context perfectly.**
 
• The second blank requires an **adjective **that** describes the price as being too high**.
 
• The word "**exorbitant**" means **unreasonably high, and is a suitable choice.**
 
• **Option 2**, "embellished; errant," is not a suitable choice as "embellished" means decorated, but it does not convey the intended meaning in this context. "Errant" means wandering or straying from the correct course, which is not related to the context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3**, "extinct; ecstatic," is not a suitable choice as "extinct" means no longer in existence, which is not related to the context of the sentence. "Ecstatic" means extremely happy or joyful, which does not convey the intended meaning in this context.
 
• **Option 4**, "erudite; enormous," is not a suitable choice as "erudite" means having or showing extensive knowledge, learning, or culture, which is not related to the context of the sentence. "Enormous" means very large, which does not convey the intended meaning in this context.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

**Correct Sentence:**__ *The blue embroidered saree is no doubt an **__exquisite__ **piece of handwork, but because of its **__exorbitant__ **price no one was ready to buy it.*

questions.question:
** Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

They __made us to wait__ while they were checking our documents.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** Made us wait.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb **"make"** is used in the **causative sense **to indicate that someone causes someone else to do something.
 
• In this context, "**made**" is already in the **past tense**, and the addition of **"to"** before **"wait"** is unnecessary and grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct way to express the causative sense of **"make" **is** to use the base form of the verb that follows it, which is "wait" in this case.** 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• She **made me clean **my room before I could go out with my friends.
 
• The teacher **made the students write** an essay on the topic.
 
• He **made his employees work** overtime to finish the project on time.
 
 
 
• **Option 2**, "made us to waits," is grammatically incorrect because the form of the verb "wait" is incorrect.
 
• **Option 3**, "make us wait," is incorrect because it is in the present tense, whereas the sentence is in the past tense.
 
• **Option 4**, "make us to waiting," is grammatically incorrect because the form of the verb "waiting" is incorrect.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

**Correct Sentence:**__ *They __**made us wai**__t while they were checking our documents.*

questions.question:
**In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.**

Burkin once had a client who had a breast tumour that was not spotted until it had __________ and she wanted to sue her internist for the delayed __________ and was also aware it was her _______ who was potentially at fault.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **M​etastasized, diagnosis, radiologist.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The context of the sentence suggests that the client had a breast tumour that was not detected in time and had spread to other parts of the body.
 
• The words that would fit best in the blanks are "**metastasized**" and "**diagnosis**."
 
• **Metastasized **refers to the spread of cancer cells from the original site of the cancer to other parts of the body. This process is called metastasis.
 
• **Diagnosis **refers to the identification or determination of the nature and cause of a particular health condition or disease based on a patient's symptoms, medical history, and physical examination, as well as diagnostic tests or procedures. 
 
• The third word would be a medical professional who may have been responsible for the delayed diagnosis.
 
• "**Radiologist**" is the most appropriate option in this context because radiologists specialize in using medical imaging techniques such as X-rays and mammograms to diagnose and treat diseases.
 
• **Example sentences:**
 
 
• **Metastasis **is the spread of cancer cells from one part of the body to another.
 
• A delayed **diagnosis **can have serious consequences for a patient's health.
 
• The **radiologist **examined the X-ray to determine the cause of the patient's symptoms.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

**Correct Sentence:__ ***Burkin once had a client who had a breast tumour that was not spotted until it had __**metastasized**__* *and she wanted to sue her internist for the delayed __**diagnosis**__* *and was also aware it was her __**radiologist**__* *who was potentially at fault.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• **Other options:**
 
• **Metamorphosed **means to undergo a transformation in form or nature.
 
 
• For example, a caterpillar **metamorphoses **into a butterfly.
 
 
 
• **Necropsy **is an autopsy performed on an animal to determine the cause of death.
 
 
• For example, a veterinarian may perform a **necropsy **on a deceased pet to determine the cause of illness.
 
 
 
• **Biopsy **is a medical procedure in which a sample of tissue is removed from the body for examination.
 
 
• For example, a **biopsy **may be performed on a suspicious mole to check for cancer cells.
 
 
 
• **Nephrologist** is a medical professional who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of kidney-related diseases.
 
• **Cardiologist**: This is a medical professional who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of heart-related diseases.
 
• The word "**metaphorised**" is not a common English word, and it is not found in most dictionaries. However, it could be interpreted as the past tense of "metaphorize," which means to use a metaphor or create a metaphorical comparison.
 
• **Autopsy**, also known as a post-mortem examination or necropsy, is a medical examination of a deceased person's body to determine the cause of death and to identify any underlying medical conditions that may have contributed to their death. 
 
• A **dermatologist **is a medical doctor who specializes in diagnosing and treating conditions and diseases related to the skin, hair, and nails. 
 
• **Metabolism **refers to the chemical processes that occur within a living organism to maintain life. When we say that a substance has been **metabolized**, it means that it has undergone chemical changes within the body as part of the metabolic process.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in a sentence.**

She __evinced__ little enthusiasm for the outdoor games.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Showed.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the sentence is **"showed" (option 1).**
 
• The word "**evinced**" means **to reveal or show (something).**
 
• Example sentences:
 
 
• The student evinced a great deal of interest in the subject matter during the lecture.
 
• The politician evinced a lack of concern for the environment in his speeches.
 
 
 
• The word "**showed**" means** to display or exhibit something**.
 
• Here are some examples:
 
 
• He **showed **me how to use the new software.
 
• She **showed **her support for the charity by donating a large sum of money.
 
 
 
• In this sentence, the word "evinced" implies that the person did not display much enthusiasm for outdoor games.
 
• Therefore,** option 1, "showed,"** is the most appropriate meaning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other options:**
 
• **Observed**: This means to watch or notice (something).
 
 
• For example, "I **observed **a strange behavior in my neighbor's cat."
 
 
 
• **Suppressed**: This means to restrain or hold back (something).
 
 
• For example, "He **suppressed **his anger and spoke calmly."
 
 
 
• **Pretended**: This means to act as if something is true when it is not.
 
 
• For example, "She **pretended **to be interested in the conversation even though she was bored."

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

“Has he come to office today?” You asked me

options.text: You asked me if he is coming to office today.
You asked me whether he is in office today.
You asked me if he has come to office today.
You asked me whether he had come to office that day.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) You asked me whether he had come to office that day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in** Direct Speech. **We need to convert it into** Indirect Speech.**
 
• **Indirect speech** is used to report what someone said, without using the exact words that were spoken. In this case, we need to report the question that was asked in indirect speech.
 
• To convert this into indirect speech, we need to change the tense of the verb **'has come'** to past perfect **'had come',** as the question was asked in the past.
 
• To make the indirect speech for questions that can be answered in **YES/NO**, the word "if" or "whether" is used before the reported speech within the sentence.
 
• We also need to change the word '**today'** to **'that day',** as we are reporting a past event.
 
• Examples of other sentences in indirect speech:
 
 
• Direct speech: "I **have finished **my work," he said.
 
• Indirect speech: He said that he **had finished** his work.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

**Therefore, the indirect speech form of the question is:*** "You asked me whether he had come to office that day."*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom.**

In two minds
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** Holding conflicting opinions.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence is **option 4: "holding conflicting opinions."**
 
• The idiom **"of two minds"** means** to be undecided or uncertain about something because one is torn between two conflicting opinions or options.**
 
• In the given sentence, the speaker is uncertain whether to go to the convention or not, indicating that he/she has conflicting thoughts or opinions about it.
 
• **Example sentences:**
 
 
• I'm **of two minds** about whether to accept the job offer or not.
 
• She was **of two minds** about buying the expensive dress, but in the end, she decided to go for it.
 
• He's **of two minds **about whether to invest in the stock market or keep his money in a savings account.
 
 
 
• **Option 1**, **"holding a negative opinion,"** is incorrect because "of two minds" does not indicate a negative opinion, but rather a state of being undecided or uncertain.
 
• **Option 2**, **"holding a clear opinion,"** is incorrect because "of two minds" implies the opposite of having a clear opinion or stance on something.
 
• **Option 3**, **"holding a positive opinion," **is incorrect for the same reason as option 2. The idiom "of two minds" does not imply a positive or negative opinion, but rather a state of uncertainty or indecision.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

The swallow asked the skylark, “Will we be able to shift the eggs from this tree by tomorrow?”

options.text: The swallow asked the skylark whether they would be able to shift the eggs from that tree by the next day.
The swallow asked the skylark whether they could be able to shift the eggs from this tree by tomorrow.
The swallow asked the skylark whether they would have been able to shift the eggs from the tree by the next day.
The swallow asked the skylark whether they will be able to shift the eggs from that tree by the next day.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **The swallow asked the skylark whether they would be able to shift the eggs from that tree by the next day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given answer is in **Direct Speech**. We need to convert it into** indirect speech.**
 
• The rules of Direct and Indirect speech for interrogative sentence conversions.
 
 
• Inverted commas are removed in indirect speech.
 
• The reporting verb **'asked'** remains the same.
 
• The first person in the reported speech changes according to the subject of reporting speech.
 
• In Reported Speech, change of the second person depends on the object of reporting speech.
 
• The third person remains unchanged.
 
• **'We'** changes to **'they'.**
 
• To make the indirect speech for questions that can be answered in YES/NO, the word **"if"** or **"whether"** is used before the reported speech within the sentence.
 
• **"Will"** changes to **"would."**
 
• **'This'** changes to** 'that'.**
 
• **'Tomorrow'** changes to **'the next day'**.
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• He said to me "Can you help me?"
 
• He asked me if I could help him.
 
 
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

**Correct Indirect Speech:**__ *The swallow asked the skylark whether they would be able to shift the eggs from that tree by the next day.*

questions.question: Select the ANTONYM of the word ‘endeavour’.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** Idleness.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct antonym of the word **‘endeavour’ **is** 'Idleness' (option 4).**
 
• **Endeavour** means** to make an effort or attempt to achieve something. **In contrast, **idleness **means **avoiding work or being lazy.**
 
• So, if someone is idle, they are not making any effort to achieve a goal, whereas if someone is making an endeavour, they are putting in the effort to achieve a goal.
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• The company's CEO is making every **endeavour **to increase profits.
 
• John's **idleness **cost him his job.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options are:
 
• **Readiness:** Readiness means being prepared or willing to do something. It is not an antonym of 'endeavour'.
 
 
• Example: The troops were in a state of **readiness **to face the enemy.
 
 
 
• **Effort: **Effort is a synonym of 'endeavour'. It means putting in the work or exertion to accomplish a goal.
 
 
• Example: She put in a lot of **effort** to pass her exams.
 
 
 
• **Selflessness:** Selflessness means putting others' needs before one's own. It is not an antonym of 'endeavour'.
 
 
• Example: The volunteers showed great **selflessness **in their work to help the victims of the flood.
